arguments.distinguishes: Both hypotheses predict the same recorded holding failure, so endpoint or physical metrics cannot separate them. Only the pattern of per-update effective_horizon together with optimization_raw_status can: persistent sub-10 horizons with budget-limited stops support the truncation account; full-horizon Solve_Succeeded updates with isolated reductions (as hinted by F450 versus F469) weaken solver.terminal_horizon_truncation and leave the saturated-budget account (controller.budget_truncated_plan_selection) as the better-supported mechanism, while a mixed pattern that co-varies horizon and status would retain both without a dominant cause. The check also confirms that the holding-speed violation (F428 > F456) is not terminal-reach related (F470 reach_passed true).

expected.observation: Across the 8 sampled update_ids the recorded effective_horizon is below the configured 10 at most sampled updates.
Across the 8 sampled update_ids the recorded effective_horizon equals the configured 10 at all but at most one update.
optimization_raw_status at most sampled updates is a budget/iteration-limited stop (e.g., User_Requested_Stop), coordinated with reduced effective_horizon.
optimization_raw_status at most sampled updates is Solve_Succeeded with full effective_horizon 10.

limitations: Controller-update evidence only, not backend motion and not a closed-loop replay; it cannot by itself establish a dominant cause.
At most 8 of 35 updates are shown per query, so behavior between sampled updates is unavailable rather than absent.
Terminal reach success (F470) is compatible with the holding-speed failure (F428 > F456); neither contradicts the other and neither is used as evidence against the checked hypotheses.
Frames are kept distinct: effective_horizon is in control intervals, tip speeds are world-frame, and solver status is a string.
missing_information: Per-update effective_horizon and optimization_raw_status for the 27 update_ids not selected; the retained controller_horizon/solver_status inventories hold 35 records and at most 8 can be shown per query.
Full historical warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are absent (control_snapshots.json not retained; full_snapshots_available F528 false).
No closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal-attribution capability exists, so no single check can certify a dominant cause.
arguments.question: In candidate execution 087adee8e8a24fe88e5c85fe89e638c8, does the recorded per-update effective_horizon show persistent truncation below the configured 10-control-interval horizon across the run, coordinated with budget-limited solver stops, so as to distinguish solver.terminal_horizon_truncation from controller.budget_truncated_plan_selection as the better-supported explanation of the unchanged holding-speed failure (F428 holding_max_speed_m_s 1.1750052670100422 m/s versus F456 limit 0.02 m/s)?

F511 (35 deadline misses), F503 (User_Requested_Stop=34), F472 (Solve_Succeeded=1), F452 (mean complete update 17.77877309145406 s against the 0.01 s control period) and F465 (first-update wall 29.352235099999234 s) indicate a saturated solve budget; the proposed query adds per-update optimization_raw_status to test budget-limited plan selection, the hypothesis' named mechanism.

stopping_conditions: Stop after the single evidence_query returns effective_horizon and optimization_raw_status for the selected update_ids.
If fewer than the requested updates are returned, treat unreturned samples as unavailable, never as evidence of truncation or saturation.
Do not escalate to a numerical check, backend execution or production change within this phase (max_checks=1 shared).
